prize_parts.citation: for the development of palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling, a general ligand-controlled method for forming aryl-nitrogen bonds
for the development of base editing, programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: I have changed my preferred configuration: I now propose B023 (Buchwald and Hartwig) with B060 (Liu alone), replacing B030 as the partner of base editing. Round 1 showed that B060 is the only candidacy carried or listed by members from several fields, and that Liu is the decisive originator in every statement that discusses it. B023 is the partner that can actually gather votes: Aqvist and Somfai place it first, Chabes and I list it as an alternative, and Aili and Zou call it a defensible fallback. It has the cleanest attribution on the shortlist, a record of more than 25 years of independent confirmation, and a mechanism understood in detail (oxidative addition, amine binding and deprotonation, reductive elimination, with ligand design controlling each step). Together the two parts are distinct achievements, a classical bond-forming method and a new programmable chemical capability in nucleic acids, and they use exactly three names, which respects the limit. I do not claim the pairing is thematically unified; it is the configuration most likely to be supported by five members while each part stands on its own scientific merit.
statement.case_against: B030 remains scientifically the case I know best, but I ranked it alone in the opening and nobody else carried it into round 1. The chair's summary shows no support for it beyond mine, and I should not let field affinity decide the matter. The remaining risks of my new configuration are real. B023 follows the 2010 cross-coupling prize and the expert report must show that C-N bond formation needed its own mechanistic insight and ligand generations, not only optimisation; the Kosugi 1983 priority must be settled in the written record because the Academy will have to justify his omission. B060 is young, its clinical record is short, long-term safety is unproven, it follows the 2020 CRISPR prize, and Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida are left out of a Liu-alone credit. The pairing is a pragmatic two-part prize, not a single theme.

responses.point: Zou asked whether B030 is a discovery or the experimental validation of Marcus theory in proteins, which the committee honoured in 1992, and what a citation would say that is not already covered.
responses.response: That is a fair challenge and I cannot answer it fully. The defensible content is the Ru-modified protein experiments, which gave the distance dependence of tunnelling through the protein medium and the role of the intervening structure, and later the case for multistep hopping. Marcus theory predicts rates for given driving force and reorganisation energy; it does not tell you how coupling decays through a folded polypeptide. Still, I cannot name one dated breakthrough, and the expert report would have to separate this from the 1992 recognition. Since you and others see it as validation, and since no one else carries it, I have moved it to an alternative.

responses.point: Linke asked what the key experimental discovery behind B030 was and in what year, and said he could support it only if paired with a more generative achievement.
responses.response: The Ru-modified protein work built through the 1980s and 1990s, with intramolecular electron transfer in ruthenium-labelled cytochrome c and later azurin, and the tunnelling-timetable and hopping syntheses from the 2000s onward. I cannot give you a single year and I will not pretend to, which is the very problem of a line of work without one attributable discovery. Your question, together with the lack of any other supporter, is why I no longer lead with it. I thank you for the question, and I also note your own B039 faces a similar difficulty of separating the pore concept, pore engineering and the enzyme ratchet, which is why I still hold it outside my configuration.

responses.point: Somfai pairs B023 with B060, arguing that C-N coupling is new chemistry relative to the 2010 C-C couplings and that Kosugi's tin-amide work was neither general nor catalytic.
responses.response: I now arrive at your configuration, and I accept your argument on both points. In round 1 I asked for the expert report to say what was new in chemical principle; your answer, that C-N bond formation required its own ligand generations and that amine binding and deprotonation change the catalytic cycle, is the kind of mechanistic distinction I wanted, and it is a stronger objection to the 2010 overlap than the one I raised. I would still put Kosugi's priority in the written record, but I agree he does not take a laureate seat. We differ on the way to describe the second part: I would stress that base editing is a designed chemical transformation, not a Cas9 extension.

responses.point: Aqvist proposes Buchwald and Hartwig alone for B023 and keeps Liu as an alternative, asking whether base editing is a chemistry prize or a downstream extension of the 2020 CRISPR prize.
responses.response: I take the question seriously and my answer is partly yours. Base editing does depend on the Cas9 platform, but what Liu's group evolved is the chemistry: a deaminase acting on single-stranded DNA exposed in the R-loop, uracil handling, and later an evolved TadA that deaminates adenosine in DNA, an activity no natural enzyme was known to have. That is a chemical outcome at one nucleotide without strand cleavage, and it differs from 2020, which honoured the programmable cutting. I accept that it is a second part, not a sole prize, and that is why I would pair it with your mature candidate rather than let it stand alone.

responses.point: Chabes pairs B060 (Liu alone) with B041 (Crews and Deshaies), arguing that both are chemistry that reprograms biology and that B041 is less covered by an earlier prize.
responses.response: I agree on Liu alone and on pairing the young candidacy with something established. Where I differ is on the partner. B041 has no approved degrader, and your own statement says that fitting it into two names leaves a visible gap on Ciulli, Handa and the cereblon strand; the committee has not decided whether the citation covers PROTACs only. B023 has no such open attribution question, so it is the safer second part. I keep B041 as an alternative and would move toward it if the reports settle the Handa and Ciulli question and show clinical validation.

uncertainties: Whether the expert report finds C-N coupling distinct enough in principle from the 2010 cross-coupling prize, and how the Kosugi priority question will be recorded.
Whether base editing is judged chemistry rather than genome biology, and whether Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID) or Komor and Gaudelli require credit.
Whether five members will accept a pragmatic two-part prize that combines a classical method with a chemical-biology tool, instead of a single strongly supported achievement.
Whether the long-range electron transfer work of Gray and Winkler deserves recognition in a later year, which I cannot resolve now.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent for the shortlisted candidates in my final configuration. My research on proton and electron transfer in respiratory enzymes is adjacent to B030, which I have moved to an alternative; I have no personal or institutional tie to Gray or Winkler, Buchwald, Hartwig or Liu. My Stockholm University colleague Xiaodong Zou is a committee member, but her configuration contains none of my named laureates.
